course_proper.bias_notes: Clockwise. A sprawling, championship-grade 2,227m oval with sweeping turns and a demanding 410m home straight featuring 'The Rise' (a steep uphill climb from the 300m to 150m mark). This uphill stretch severely tests stamina—one-dimensional leaders often weaken, allowing strong closers ('Swoopers') and mid-pack stalkers fair opportunities.
course_proper.post_bias: Fair from most starts when rail is True. In 1000m-1200m sprints, middle-to-inside draws (1-6) are preferred. In 1400m-1600m races, wide barriers (10+) force horses to work hard early to avoid being trapped wide around the sweep into the straight.

kensington_track.bias_notes: Clockwise inner track. Much tighter, sharper turns with a short 301m home straight. Plays with a strong natural bias toward on-pace runners and 'box-seat' stalkers. Deep closers are at a severe disadvantage unless an unmanageable pace duel develops up front.
kensington_track.post_bias: Inside barriers (1-4) hold a significant advantage. Wide draws (8+) are heavily penalized in short sprints as horses get trapped 3-wide without cover on tight turns.

handicapping_angles.the_rise_stamina_test: On the Course Proper, ensure horses entering the 300m mark have proven L200 (last 200m) strength. The steep uphill climb at 'The Rise' causes weak leaders to hit the wall hard.
handicapping_angles.kensington_leader_boost: When racing is on the Kensington inner track, aggressively upgrade front-runners ('E') and box-seat stalkers ('P'). Heavily downgrade wide-drawn closers.
handicapping_angles.wet_track_outside_lane: On Soft 7 to Heavy 10 tracks, the inside 2-3 paths on the Course Proper often break down into a bog. Look for jockeys fanning wide (4-8 paths off the rail) to find the 'Fast Lane' down the outside fence.
handicapping_angles.rail_position_exaggerator: When the rail is moved out +6m or beyond on the Course Proper, the turn geometry narrows and heavily favors horses racing on the speed or along the inside rail.
handicapping_angles.australian_weight_bifurcation: In Handicap/Benchmark races (BM64-BM88), penalize top-weight runners carrying 59kg+ (1kg = ~1 length). In Group/WFA (Weight-For-Age) company, disregard weight and prioritize pure class and peak rating.
